description: Claims about Nebius Token Factory inference, each with source, date, tag and (for vendor, third-party and report claims) the workload. Docs entries are dated by fetch day.

entries.claim: Two flavors, Base and Fast, give identical model outputs. Fast uses smaller batches, more compute and speculative decoding. Select it by appending -fast to the model name.
Documented optimisations: KV cache, paged attention, flash attention, quantization, continuous batching, context caching, speculative decoding. Engine and version are not named.
The API accepts the full set of vLLM parameters; the Playground only the common ones.
Dedicated endpoint fields: gpu_type, gpu_count per replica, region (eu-north1, eu-west1, us-central1), scaling.min_replicas and max_replicas, enabled. Total max GPUs is gpu_count times max_replicas.
Endpoint region cannot be updated after creation. Scaling changes can trigger provisioning of extra replicas with a warm-up period.

Minimum replicas are reserved and non-preemptible only while the endpoint is active. Scaling above minimum depends on burst capacity. Stopping releases GPUs to a shared pool. No formal SLA unless covered by contract.
Custom model weights on dedicated endpoints are in beta and available on request.
Fine-tuned models (LoRA or full) deploy only via Dedicated endpoints. MoE LoRA adapters must be merged into the exact base weights before deployment.

Custom speculator jobs use method spec-draft. Architectures: eagle3 (Token Factory only) and eagle3_original (portable to vLLM). Losses kl, lk_alpha, lk_hybrid. Reported metrics include acceptance_rate and number_of_tokens per head.
A trained drafter is served in vLLM through --speculative-config. Eagle heads share weights, so num_speculative_tokens can be set from 1 to N and should be tuned to the observed acceptance.

Dynamic rate limits: rolling 15-minute windows, x1.2 at 80 percent usage or more, divide by 1.5 at 50 percent or less, hard ceiling 20x base. Over-limit requests may be served at lower priority with x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes.
service_tier values: auto, default, over-limit, flex, no-limit. Flex does not consume rate-limit credits, runs at lower priority and can still return 429.

Inference Observability metrics exist only for Dedicated Endpoints: traffic, KV-cache hit rate (local and external hits), p50/p90/p99 latency, TTFT on streaming only, active replicas, GPU utilisation average and busiest, errors by status code.

Observability data is collected in the region where inference runs but stored in eu-north. Metrics are exposed through a Prometheus federate endpoint on read.monitoring.api.nebius.cloud, scrape interval 15 seconds or more.
Cached tokens are best effort. A repeat request can return cached_tokens 0 after eviction, on a different replica, or after a model or service update. The value is rounded down to a block boundary.
On Serverless the cache is shared within a model across customers. On Dedicated Endpoints each customer has an isolated cache. prompt_cache_key only helps route to the server that holds the cache.
Public serverless shows region Global. Processing location can change at any time without notice. Not intended for production that needs a stable region.
Dedicated endpoints use no multi-region routing, load balancing or automatic overflow or failover to other regions.
By default inputs and outputs may be stored and used for speculative decoding, in Finland. Zero Data Retention opts out and may reduce inference speed.

Serverless models are removed on fixed dates (2026-06-22, 2026-08-31, 2026-11-09) with no automatic rerouting. Dedicated endpoints for the same models are unaffected. June removals included several -fast variants.
Structured output supports json_object and json_schema. Support differs per model because of training data or inference engine limits.
Function calling is controlled by tool_choice. Model support differs.

OpenAPI 20261109: ModelFlavor has a quantization field; GPU enum includes B200 and B300 variants; reservation_policy AUTO, FORBID, STRICT; routing_key starts with dedicated/ and is 12 to 128 characters.
Status enum starting, running, updating, stopping, stopped, error. Readiness enum ready, partially_ready, not_ready. The deployment object returns ready_replicas.

The rate-limit page points to a Batch API with higher limits and Data Lab lists batch inference outputs. The published OpenAPI has no /v1/batches path, so the batch contract is a documentation gap. Cached-token pricing excludes batch.
Fine-tuning jobs support LoRA and full-parameter training. Checkpoints include adapter_config.json for LoRA.
Data Lab collects inference logs (inputs and outputs) unless Zero Data Retention is enabled, and processes them in EU-North1.

The 2026-08-19 us-central1 incident made Token Factory models in that region partially or fully unavailable from 10:37 UTC until 20:25 UTC. Capacity outside the region kept serving but depends on us-central1 for deployment and scaling operations.

Cache-aware routing versus default Kubernetes ClusterIP routing: average step time 4.8 s against 9.0 s, p95 17 s against 70.8 s, token cache share about 95 percent against 62 percent. A standalone load-aware baseline was not tested.
entries.workload: SWE-style agent trajectories, devstral-2-small-2512, 300 concurrent, 3 vLLM replicas, 6 runs

entries.claim: Chat proof of concept: cache hit rate rose from about 5 percent to 50 to 60 percent with cache-aware routing and larger per-GPU buffers; Nebius states about four times lower cost.
entries.workload: anonymised conversational platform, 70B chat model, mirrored production traffic

entries.claim: Chat proof of concept used prefill-specialised and decode-specialised workers, locality-first routing and backpressure; four B200 GPUs sustained about 10 RPS.
entries.workload: anonymised conversational platform, 70B chat model, controlled tests

entries.claim: Chat proof of concept failure classes: invalid decode-worker states, KV-cache corruption fixed by a TensorRT-LLM upgrade, retry storms, router queue saturation, aggressive liveness probes, logging overload.
entries.workload: anonymised conversational platform, pre-production proof of concept

entries.claim: An FP4 checkpoint changed chat behaviour (shorter replies, more repetition, empty outputs); Nebius re-quantised with real sessions and tested FP8 against BF16 KV cache. Chat-specific alerts cover tail TTFT, cache drops, finish_reason drift and decode error bursts.
entries.workload: anonymised conversational platform, 70B chat model, A/B signals

entries.claim: Same post states a 99.9 percent SLA for dedicated endpoints and zero-retention inference. The docs say no formal SLA without a contract and that retention is on by default.
entries.workload: anonymised conversational platform deployment under contract

entries.claim: Shared KV cache tier (WEKA Augmented Memory Grid over RDMA) against HBM-only: 93 percent against 40 percent hit rate, 2.4x requests served, TTFT p95 3.82 s against 23.12 s.
entries.workload: 8-hour replay of agentic coding sessions, DeepSeek-V4-Pro NVFP4, one 8x B300 node, vLLM v0.23, 512 active sessions

entries.claim: Sticky routing raised exact prefix reuse from 48 to about 96 percent (+17.1 percent throughput). FP8 KV storage gave +55.7 percent throughput. Cache offload cost 3.1 to 7.8 percent throughput.
entries.workload: agentic RL rollouts, GLM-5.2, four B300 nodes, 1,024 matched trajectories

entries.claim: LK losses train drafters to maximise acceptance rate directly instead of KL divergence, reported better across 8B to 685B targets.
entries.workload: drafter training, MT-bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, vLLM with patched rejection sampling

entries.claim: SlimSpec cuts the drafter LM-head cost by 4 to 5x against the full projection while keeping acceptance competitive.
entries.workload: EAGLE-3 drafters, Llama-3.1-8B, batch sizes 1 and 64, vLLM 0.17.1, H200

entries.claim: Custom Speculator Training launched 2026-06-25. Drafters attach to a Dedicated Endpoint and deployment is reviewed by solutions engineers at launch.
entries.workload: workload-specific drafters on Dedicated Endpoints, launch announcement

entries.claim: Speculative decoding is argued to cut full-model decode steps and so tail latency for long-context non-streaming MoE use. No measured numbers given.
entries.workload: large MoE models, long-context non-streaming products, conceptual argument

entries.claim: NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX is coming to Token Factory for a subset of models with the same autoscaling and observability. 3,400 output tokens per second single user, benchmarked by Artificial Analysis.
entries.workload: Gemma 4 31B, single user, Groq 3 LPX

entries.claim: Eigen AI co-develops optimised open models for Token Factory. Up to 911 output tokens per second per Artificial Analysis as of 2026-03-13.
entries.workload: GPT-OSS-120B output speed on Artificial Analysis, Eigen-optimised serving

entries.claim: Clarifai is described as strengthening the system layer: serving, orchestration, hardware support, reliability. Eigen AI strengthens the model and runtime layer.
entries.workload: company strategy statement, no workload

entries.claim: MLPerf Inference v6.1: five first places in 20 entries; Vera Rubin NVL72 preview on DeepSeek R1 at 16,427 tokens/s per GPU (server). These measure Nebius AI Cloud systems, not the Token Factory data plane.
entries.workload: MLPerf Inference v6.1 server scenario, DeepSeek R1, 36 GPUs, preview category

entries.claim: MLPerf Inference v5.1: virtual GPU instances run without virtualising the GPU or ConnectX adapters, claimed to match bare metal.
entries.workload: MLPerf Inference v5.1, Llama 2 70B and Llama 3.1 405B, single host

entries.claim: Dedicated Endpoints: control plane API and region-specific data plane scale independently. Example 70B deployment on 2 H100 per replica, min 2, max 8.
entries.workload: illustrative 70B configuration, no measured result

entries.claim: Launch release lists a 99.9 percent SLA for dedicated endpoints, sub-second latency and up to 70 percent cost reduction through fine-tuning and distillation.
entries.workload: press release, no workload stated

entries.claim: Inference Frontier Program frames inference in three layers: engine, fleet, production reality. It names batching, KV and prefix caching, quantization, speculative decoding, routing, multi-tenant isolation.
entries.workload: community programme announcement, no measurements

entries.claim: LK losses were contributed to SpecForge as a merged pull request (number 492).
Hugging Face org nebius publishes EAGLE3 drafters for Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.3 70B, gpt-oss-20b, gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3-235B, plus Medusa, MLP-Speculator and MTP variants.
The github.com/nebius org has no fork or repo of vLLM, SGLang, LMCache, llm-d, Dynamo or TensorRT-LLM. Inference-related repos are token-factory-cookbook, tokenfactory-rl and kvax.
A Nebius-affiliated author (profile company @nebius) merged a vLLM docs guide for Nebius Serverless AI. This is the AI Cloud serverless product, not Token Factory.
Open vLLM issue: nebius/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b gives corrupted greedy output at 5 or more speculative tokens, correct with --enforce-eager.
entries.workload: gpt-oss-20b on AMD MI355X, vLLM, single reporter, unconfirmed by maintainers

entries.claim: SemiAnalysis InferenceX credits Nebius as a compute supporter. No Nebius-ranked inference result was found.
entries.workload: benchmark programme, web-search summary of the project README, page not read in full

entries.claim: A web search surfaced a job listing naming speculative decoding, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching and disaggregated prefill and decode as Token Factory work. Not fetched.
